clue.text: Rocks regularly seen in circle

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word circle, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Stones placed at even intervals are seen forming a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' suggests stones; it is the drinks sense, as in whisky on the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink served on the rocks comes over frozen cubes, so rocks is slang for frozen water.

clue.text: So you can do it right, Nero fiddled

indicators.note: fiddled means tampered with or rearranged, so the letters before it are reworked

explanation.surface: Nero, famously fiddling, is told how to perform it correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' rearranges DOIT, R and NERO; the nod is to Nero fiddling while Rome burned.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a purpose: you do one thing so as to make another possible.

clue.text: Grant a death that's painful

parts.note: a death is an end
ow is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: Someone named Grant suffers a painful death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a man's name; it is the verb, to bestow.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant funds or property to someone, especially permanently, is to endow them.

clue.text: After swapping starters, didn't bite sandwiches?

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words of the phrase trade places

parts.note: a weak drink or remark lacked punch, that is, didn't bite
second word of the same phrase

explanation.surface: Someone who swapped first courses and then didn't touch the sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' pretends to be first courses; here it means the opening letters of the two words, which trade places to turn a feeble effort into a lunchbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandwiches are the typical contents of a meal prepared at home and carried to work or school.

clue.text: Illusionist spirited away, then turning up pointlessly

indicators.note: away in the sense of off or gone astray tells us to scramble the word spirited
in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top
pointlessly removes a compass point, here N for north

parts.note: turning means rotating

explanation.surface: A conjuror is spirited off and then reappears without any point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ROTATIG, the turning word once 'pointlessly' has dropped its N, to make GITATOR. 'spirited away' reads as vanishing by magic, which suits the conjuror.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestidigitator is a conjuror doing sleight of hand, a performer of magic tricks.

clue.text: Old farms, some of the best for cattle rearing

indicators.note: rearing in a down entry suggests rising up, so the run of letters is read upwards
some of signals that only a run of letters inside the words is used

explanation.surface: A remark on the finest traditional smallholdings for raising livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' takes STFORC from 'best for cattle' and 'rearing' turns it round. 'cattle rearing' reads as farming but is two separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented smallholding of the Scottish Highlands, a traditional form of farm.

clue.text: Chopped wood? That contains 1000 ends

indicators.note: contains puts the thousand inside the former trees

parts.note: chopped wood is made of what were once trees, so ex-trees
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A question about firewood, then a claim that it holds a thousand offcuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopped wood was once trees, so it is EX-TREES; M goes inside. 'ends' looks like leftover bits of wood but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremes are the furthest points at either side, the limits or tips of something.

clue.text: Pathetically mortal, a credible politician

indicators.note: pathetically means in a pitiful way, a sign that the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A believable politician who is pitifully human.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pathetically' rearranges the letters of MORTAL A CREDIBLE. The party is a British one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal Democrat is a member of the British centrist party, so is a party politician.

clue.text: Number shot in us state at night

indicators.note: in places the go inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
a shot is a go or try, a turn

explanation.surface: A firearm is fired somewhere in America after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire; it means a go, a TURN. 'us' is the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal describes what happens or is active after dark, like owls.

clue.text: Orthodox Jew can identify himself

explanation.surface: A strictly observant Jewish man is able to prove who he is.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as two words: he has ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a member of a strict Jewish mystical movement; one who carries papers has identification.

clue.text: Different people read about mounted jockeys

indicators.note: about turns the word round

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to do it

indicators.note: jockeys as a verb means manoeuvres or shuffles about, so the letters move

explanation.surface: Some unusual folk read up about jockeys on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DO into OD; 'jockeys' rearranges MOUNTED. 'mounted jockeys' reads as riders on horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who are odd ones out are people unlike or excluded from the rest of a group.

clue.text: County gets us money

explanation.surface: A shire receives American cash.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCKS is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county; 'us' is the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckinghamshire is commonly shortened to this; dollars are slangily called bucks in the States.

clue.text: The responsibility of those crushed completely

parts.note: if something is down to you it is your responsibility
the ground ones are those crushed to powder

explanation.surface: Whose job it is to look after those crushed underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' looks like defeated people; it is ground, as coffee is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that suits you to a tee suits you totally, thoroughly, in every way.

clue.text: Lodge shares identical houses

indicators.note: houses as a verb means contains, so the letters are found within the words

explanation.surface: A lodge whose stakeholders all occupy identical buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to live somewhere. 'houses' is a verb, not buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to live or dwell there, usually in rented rooms.

clue.text: Crush to smaller bits?

parts.note: the clue reads as breaking something into fragments, but the sense is flattening or overpowering opposition as a heavy road machine does

explanation.definitionFit: To flatten opposition by sheer force is to bulldoze or crush it like a road vehicle.

clue.text: Scoff sandwiches left in box in aircraft

indicators.note: sandwiches as a verb means encloses between two layers

parts.note: to scoff is to jeer

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the box

parts.note: a tin is a box

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs sandwiches left in a lunch box on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' suggests eating; it means mock, JEER. 'sandwiches' is the container signal, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetliner is a large passenger plane powered by jet engines.

clue.text: Mysterious figure reportedly tied in knots

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so we want a word heard rather than written

parts.note: to figure is to reckon, to think or calculate

indicators.note: in knots means tangled, so the word tied is scrambled

explanation.surface: A puzzling character is said to be all tangled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives RECON from RECKON; 'in knots' rearranges TIED as DITE. 'figure' looks like a person but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means obscure, little known or hard to understand.

clue.text: Wild as a murderer in escape heading north

indicators.note: heading north in a down entry means the letters read upwards
in places the murderer inside the escape

parts.note: on the lam is US slang for escape, fleeing
Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: Frenzied, like a killer fleeing to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns LACAINAM, the whole container, upwards. Being on the lam is American slang for being on the run; Cain is the first murderer in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Maniacal means frenzied or crazed, as a madman behaves.

clue.text: Excessively happy, as priest in attempt to turn boy

indicators.note: to turn reverses the letters of the attempt with its priest inside
in places the priest inside the attempt

parts.note: a go is an attempt
Rev is short for Reverend, a priest's title
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A priest overjoyed at trying to convert a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses GREVO, the attempt with its priest inside, giving OVERG. 'turn' suggests a priest converting a boy, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Over- as a prefix means too much, so this is being too joyful or elated.

clue.text: Call back company writer

parts.note: to bell is to ring or call someone on the phone

indicators.note: back turns the abbreviation for company round

explanation.surface: Ring the firm's writer back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the company abbreviation to OC. Hilaire Belloc was an Anglo-French author famous for his cautionary verses for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc was a poet, essayist and author of comic verses for children.

clue.text: Reptile, one suitable for children, in good stories

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in places the film rating inside the other pieces

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories
U is the British film rating for universal, fit for all ages

explanation.surface: A lizard character is fit for children in good tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places U inside G and ANA, after I. U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguana is a large lizard found in tropical America.

clue.text: Item off a lot

parts.note: an item is a thing, something
food that is off is rotten

explanation.surface: An item removed from an auction lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lot' suggests an auction item; the definition is the British idiom, as in 'I miss you something rotten'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this phrase for very much, intensely, as in missing someone badly.

clue.text: Film following 5 in Sunday sitcom

indicators.note: following puts the film after the first and last letters
5 refers to the answer at 5 down, the ends or extremes, so take the first and last letters

parts.note: Kes is a 1969 Ken Loach film about a boy and a kestrel

explanation.surface: A film shown after five o'clock in a Sunday comedy slot.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' stands for the answer at 5 down, the ends of 'Sunday', S and Y; KES follows. SYKES was a BBC sitcom starring Eric Sykes.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a BBC situation comedy starring Eric Sykes and Hattie Jacques.

clue.text: Heads for the opera, so chooses an opera

indicators.note: heads for means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for the opera house and picks an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads for' looks like setting off; it takes the first letters of 'the opera so chooses an'. Puccini wrote TOSCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's opera about a singer, her painter lover and a police chief.

clue.text: Whip is not a thing you can hear

indicators.note: you can hear means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: nowt is northern English for nothing, not a thing

explanation.surface: A claim that a whip is silent.
explanation.walkthrough: NOWT is northern English dialect for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout was a leather scourge used for flogging in Imperial Russia.

clue.text: Orderly fellow runs behind one?

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
ass is slang for a person's behind
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A neat man jogs behind someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like an adjective; it is the noun, an attendant. A chaprassi was an Indian office messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: In British India a chaprassi was an official messenger or attendant, a servant who carried messages.

clue.text: Isn't "all free" a version of "independent"?

indicators.note: a version of implies a rearrangement of the quoted letters into another form

explanation.surface: A question whether all free is just another way to say independent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a version of' rearranges the letters of ISNT and ALLFREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who depends on no one else for support is autonomous and standing on their own feet.

clue.text: A gas fire

parts.note: Xe is the chemical symbol for xenon, a noble gas

explanation.surface: A gas fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like a heater; it means to dismiss from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone is to sack them, which is giving them the chop.
